title: Simulation Task
description: Develop a multi-agent simulation system that models the spread of mask-wearing behavior through social networks.
simulation_focus: Predict agents' mask-wearing behavior over day 30 - day 39 (last ten days) based on their attributes, social connections, and past behavior
Model information propagation and behavioral changes triggered by social influence and government intervention starting on Day 10

data_files.agent_attributes.csv: Contains demographic and behavioral attributes of each agent, including age, occupation, risk perception, and social connection counts
data_files.social_network.json: Contains structured data representing a social network. Each entry corresponds to a user (identified by a unique integer ID), and the values describe the different types of relationships that user has with others. Data Structure: The top-level structure is a dictionary ({} in JSON). Keys: Each key is a unique user ID (as an integer, e.g., 0, 1, 2, etc.). Values: Each value is another dictionary with the following fields: "family": a list of user IDs representing family connections. "work_school": a list of user IDs representing colleagues or schoolmates. "community": a list of user IDs representing community-level acquaintances. "all": a merged list of all user IDs connected to the user across the three categories above.
data_files.train_data.csv: Time series data for the first 30 days, used for training the model

RMSE.description: Root Mean Square Error measuring overall predictive accuracy of mask adoption rates
RMSE.interpretation: Directly interpretable as percentage deviations due to the 0-1 range

interactions.name: social_peer_influence
interactions.description: Agents observe peers’ mask-wearing in their social network and update attitudes and adoption based on thresholds and influence weights.

interactions.name: policy_compliance_enforcement
interactions.description: Government and locations impose mask requirements; agents decide to comply based on propensity and perceived enforcement, with possible penalties.

interactions.name: information_diffusion
interactions.description: Media broadcasts messages affecting agents’ risk perception and attitudes; government guidance also shifts perceptions.

interactions.name: supply_and_purchase
interactions.description: Agents purchase masks subject to retailer stock and price; affordability and availability affect adoption.

interactions.name: mobility_and_contact
interactions.description: Agents visit locations (workplace, school, public venues), encountering enforcement and social cues that affect mask decisions.

interactions.name: intra_household_influence
interactions.description: Household members influence each other’s mask-wearing and can share mask inventory.

metrics.name: RMSE_adoption
metrics.description: Root Mean Squared Error between simulated and observed adoption rates over the calibration period.

metrics.name: MAE_adoption
metrics.description: Mean Absolute Error between simulated and observed adoption rates over the calibration period.

metrics.name: peak_adoption
metrics.description: Maximum proportion of the population wearing masks at any time step.

metrics.name: time_to_50_percent
metrics.description: Number of days from start until adoption first reaches 50%.

metrics.name: final_adoption
metrics.description: Adoption rate on the final simulation day.

metrics.name: adoption_inequality_gini
metrics.description: Gini coefficient of adoption across demographic groups at a specified time.

validation_criteria.name: goodness_of_fit_threshold
validation_criteria.description: Calibration is accepted if RMSE_adoption is below a predefined threshold (to be specified based on data scale).

validation_criteria.name: convergence_criterion
validation_criteria.description: Calibration terminates when improvement in the objective metric is less than calibration_tolerance over successive iterations.

validation_criteria.name: parameter_bounds_check
validation_criteria.description: All calibrated parameters must remain within predefined plausible ranges (e.g., [0,1] for probabilities).

validation_criteria.name: out_of_sample_validation
validation_criteria.description: Model maintains acceptable error (e.g., MAE_adoption within threshold) on the validation period.
